$comment: Per-host SPKI pins for the MASQUE/WARP edges. Loaded by aether::trust and
validated by trust::active_pins() at startup: a host with zero unexpired
pins is a hard error, never a fallback to 'trust everyone'.
WHY BOTH PINS ARE LISTED UNDER EACH HOST: the two digests below are lifted
verbatim from consts.rs::MASQUE_PINS, where today they form one global set.
The audit defect being fixed is that the set replaced certificate
validation entirely (no chain, no validity period, no hostname) - not that
it was shared between the two Cloudflare hostnames. Splitting the digests
across hosts from an armchair would risk rejecting a live peer on a guess,
so the split is left as an explicitly measured task: observe the leaf each
SNI actually presents, then narrow. require_hostname stays false for the
same reason - the peer is dialled by IP, so tightening it needs a live
verification pass first (T065/T067).
require_chain IS NOT OPTIONAL. The field lost its serde default because an
omitted key decoded to false, which silently discarded BoringSSL's chain
verdict on every live connection while the file appeared to declare a
policy. Every host below therefore states it.
Why both still say false, and what has to happen first: each host pins the
self-signed masque leaf AND the WE1-issued cloudflareaccess.com leaf. The
self-signed one has no chain to validate, so setting require_chain=true on
either host rejects whichever edge presents it - a guaranteed outage rather
than a tightening. require_chain=true belongs on the host once the measured
split above has moved the self-signed digest off it, leaving a host whose
pins are all chain-issued. That edit is a data change to this file, which is
the point of making the field required.

pins.note: masque.cloudflareclient.com leaf, self-signed by Cloudflare - no chain exists to validate, which is why require_chain is still false for this host
cloudflareaccess.com leaf, issued by Google Trust Services WE1 - the pin whose host can take require_chain=true once the leaves are measured and split
cloudflareaccess.com leaf, issued by Google Trust Services WE1
